chunk_findings.detail: `command_provenance` decides whether the last writer of `[gate.<id>].command` was the committed or the local layer by *position* in the list: `is_local = n >= len(paths) // 2`. That is only correct when `tomlcfg.config_paths(root, "gates.toml")` returns exactly two equal, fixed halves laid out committed-then-local. It breaks for any other shape, and the required evidence schema shows a third layer exists: the failing-first test must record `command_layer` ∈ `'committed' | 'local' | 'env'`, yet this function can only ever return `'committed'` or `'local'` (`layer` is assigned only those two literals, default `"committed"`). So an env-layer command is always mislabelled. Concretely, with the list `[.ddflow/config.toml, .ddflow/gates.toml, <env-provided gates file>, .ddflow/local/config.toml, .ddflow/local/gates.toml]` (`len == 5`, `len//2 == 2`), the env path at index 2 satisfies `n >= 2`, so a pass whose command came from the environment layer records `command_layer: "local"` instead of `"env"` and the renderer prints "passed with a local-only command (not the committed one)" for a pass that is not a local-layer pass at all — the exact class of provenance mislabelling B924bdc92d7 is about, just with `env` instead of `local`. The same positional assumption also misfires on any odd-length list: if `config_paths` omits non-existent files (the `if not Path(path).is_file(): continue` guard in this very function implies paths may be filtered/absent), a repo with only the committed `.ddflow/config.toml` present yields `len(paths) == 1`, `len//2 == 0`, so index 0 gets `is_local = True` and a plain committed-command pass is reported as a local-only pass (and `committed_command` stays `""`), failing the "nothing extra for a committed-command pass" requirement. The layer should be taken from the layer identity recorded while overlaying (as the intent states), not inferred from the index. Note the README hunk itself documents only `"local"` (else `"committed"`), consistent with
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/defs.py:command_provenance

chunk_findings.detail: The "differs" clause is decided by the *presence* of `ev["committed_command_digest"]`, never by comparing it against the pass's own `command_digest`, even though the function's docstring promises it fires only "when the evidence shows the committed layer defined a **different** one". Concretely: committed config sets `[gate.unit_tests].command = "pytest -q"`, and a user's `.ddflow/local/config.toml` sets the identical string `"pytest -q"` (a common thing to do when copying the committed command into a local file that also adjusts thresholds). The overlay in `defs.py` then marks `command_layer = "local"` (the local layer is the last to set it), the runner records `command_digest` for `"pytest -q"` and `committed_command_digest` for the identical committed string, and this function appends `"; the committed command differs"` to a pass whose command is byte-for-byte the committed command — a false provenance claim of exactly the kind B924bdc92d7 is meant to eliminate. Conversely, if the runner records only the additive keys named in the change description (`command_layer`, `command_digest`, `output_log_host`) and no `committed_command_digest`, the clause is dead code and regression-test assertion (3) ("the label says the committed command differs") can never pass. Either way the function needs to compare `ev.get("command_digest") != ev.get("committed_command_digest")` (or whatever key the runner actually writes) rather than testing key existence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/outcomes.py — `_local_command_notes`

chunk_findings.detail: `command_provenance` decides which layer a command came from by the *position* of the path in `tomlcfg.config_paths`, not by the path itself: it assumes the list is exactly two equal halves (committed first, local second). Whenever that shape does not hold, a team-policy command is reported as a local one. Concrete input: a checkout for which `config_paths(root, "gates.toml")` yields three entries — e.g. `.ddflow/config.toml`, `.ddflow/gates.toml`, `.ddflow/local/config.toml` (local `gates.toml` absent from the list, or any extra layer such as the org/global layer this project is heading toward). Then `len(paths)//2 == 1`, so the committed `.ddflow/gates.toml` at `n == 1` satisfies `1 >= 1`, `is_local` becomes `True`, and the function returns `("local", "")` for a gate whose `command` is defined in the committed `.ddflow/gates.toml`. The pass is consequently rendered as "passed with a local-only command (not the committed one)" and `ddflow complete` emits the new `gate <g> …` warning (`services/completion.py`), for every user, even though the command is team policy — i.e. the same class of mislabelling B924bdc92d7 is trying to fix, just inverted. Because the committed-command capture (`if not is_local: committed = cmd`) uses the same boundary, `committed_command_digest` is also empty in that case. Classifying by the path itself (e.g. whether it lives under `.ddflow/local/`) or recording the layer inside `load_gates`, where the layer is actually known, avoids the positional assumption.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/defs.py `command_provenance` (`is_local = n >= len(paths) // 2`)

chunk_findings.detail: A local layer that sets the *same* command string as the committed layer still yields `command_layer == "local"`, but the guard `committed != gdef.command` is false, so `committed_command_digest` is omitted. The resulting evidence is indistinguishable from "the committed layer defines no command at all", and any consumer that selects the required label on `command_layer == "local"` (the intent's requirement 2 wording: label the pass "with its command taken from the local layer") will print `passed with a local-only command (not the committed one)` for a pass whose command is *exactly* the committed command — the parenthetical is false. Concrete input: committed `.ddflow/config.toml` has `[gate.unit_tests] command = "pytest -q"` and a user's `.ddflow/local/config.toml` also has `[gate.unit_tests] command = "pytest -q"` (e.g. copied while pinning a timeout); the run records `command_layer="local"`, no `committed_command_digest`, and teammates/`complete` see the "not the committed one" label even though the command that ran is byte-identical to the committed one. Either record the committed digest unconditionally (letting the renderer compare `command_digest` vs `committed_command_digest`) or record an explicit "commands identical" signal so the status can stay silent for this case, as requirement 2 demands for a pass whose command matches the project's.

chunk_findings.detail: The new evidence key `command_digest` is computed on `gdef.command`, i.e. the *un-redacted* command string, and is then written into the evidence that is shared with other users (the very premise of B924bdc92d7: bob reads Alice's pass). The intent notes that the command *text* "keeps going through the redactor as today", so a secret embedded in a local-only command is stripped from `evidence["command"]` — but the digest still commits to the raw bytes, and it cannot be salted (the status renderer has to compare the pass's `command_digest` against a `committed_command_digest` recomputed on another machine), so it is a stable pure function of the command. Concrete case: Alice's git-ignored `.ddflow/local/config.toml` sets `[gate.unit_tests].command = "pytest --api-token sk-live-…"`; her pass evidence shows a redacted `command` but ships `command_digest`; any other user who can read the pass evidence (or a log into which the evidence was rendered) knows the command template and can brute-force/confirm candidate tokens offline with `digest("pytest --api-token <candidate>") == command_digest`, exactly the disclosure the redactor exists to prevent. Line 103 should digest the redacted command text (or the digest should be computed by a redaction-aware helper and only for commands whose layer has no local secret), so the fingerprint cannot be used as an oracle for a value the redactor removed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/runner.py:103 (`command_layer_evidence`, `ev["command_digest"] = digest(gdef.command)`)

data.probe: command_digest is blake2b-8 (64 bits, 16 hex) of the command string -- the digest the bug record requires, comparable across machines, so it cannot be salted or computed over a per-machine redaction. Probe: blake2b-8('pytest --api-token sk-live-'+40 random chars)=9e1b9a8fdf37e57a; recovering a high-entropy token needs guessing it, and ddflow already ships output_digest/tree_sha of the same class. Secrets belong in [gate].env, not the command line; no code change.
